quizzes.title: Trophies, FIFA and Title Winners: MCQ
quizzes.passage:
FIFA is the global governing body for football, and it has member national associations. The World Cup has used two trophies in its history. The first was the Jules Rimet Trophy, which was in use from 1930 to 1970. It was made of gold-plated sterling silver and stood on a lapis lazuli base. The original trophy was stolen in England before the 1966 tournament and was later found in a rubbish heap. It was stolen a second time and is believed to have been melted down.

Since 1974 the tournament has used a different trophy. It depicts two human figures holding up the Earth. Winners do not keep it permanently, because it remains in the possession of FIFA and can no longer be won outright. Winners receive a replica instead.

Individual honours also accompany the tournament. The Golden Ball goes to the best player, the Golden Glove to the best goalkeeper, and the Young Player Award to the best young player. The Golden Boot goes to the player who scores the most goals, and the FIFA Fair Play Trophy is presented to one team. Separately, a Women's World Cup began in 1991, and its 2023 edition was hosted by Australia and New Zealand.

questions.q: Who designed the current FIFA World Cup trophy?
questions.explanation: The booklet names Italian sculptor Silvio Gazzaniga as the designer of the current trophy.

questions.q: What was the name of the dog that found the stolen Jules Rimet Trophy?
questions.explanation: The original trophy was found in a rubbish heap by a dog called Pickles.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Brazil was allowed to keep the Jules Rimet Trophy after its 1970 win.
Reason (R): Brazil won the Jules Rimet Trophy outright in 1970.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Brazil was allowed to keep the trophy because it won it outright in 1970.

questions.q:

II. West Germany
III. Brazil
IV. Donald Trump
A. First team to lift the current trophy
B. Won the Jules Rimet Trophy outright in 1970

questions.explanation: Barassi hid the original trophy, West Germany lifted the current one first, Brazil won it outright in 1970, and Trump was the inaugural Peace Prize recipient.

questions.q:
I. The current trophy was chosen from 53 submitted proposals.
II. The current trophy was first lifted by Brazil in 1974.
III. The current trophy is made of 18-carat solid gold.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: The design was chosen from 53 proposals and the trophy is 18-carat gold, but West Germany, not Brazil, lifted it first.

questions.q:
I. FIFA's headquarters is located in Zurich, Switzerland.
II. The FIFA Peace Prize was established in 2024.
III. The Jules Rimet Trophy was created by an Italian sculptor.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the Peace Prize dates from 2025 and the Jules Rimet Trophy was made by a French sculptor.

questions.q: Which two countries are the only ones to have retained the World Cup title?
questions.explanation: Italy and Brazil are the only two countries to have retained the trophy.

questions.q: In which city is FIFA's headquarters located? (city)

questions.q: What was the name of the dog that found the stolen Jules Rimet Trophy? (name)

quizzes.title: Records and Firsts: MCQ
quizzes.passage:
The 2026 FIFA World Cup was the 23rd men's edition, and it was staged across three countries: the United States, Canada and Mexico. It was the first time three nations jointly hosted the event. The competition featured 48 teams, divided into 12 groups of four, and a total of 104 matches were played. The official match ball was the Adidas Trionda.

The first edition was held in 1930. The World Cup has been held every four years, apart from 1942 and 1946. Four nations made their World Cup debut in 2026: Cape Verde, Curaçao, Jordan and Uzbekistan. Cape Verde is a tiny archipelago off the west coast of Africa, and its population is about half a million people.

Several milestones were recorded during the tournament, and several of them are described as firsts in the history of the competition. Cape Verde's 40-year-old veteran goalkeeper, Vozinha, emerged as one of the breakout stars of the tournament.

The tournament had controversies. Iran moved its base camp to Mexico, which meant long travel to the United States for its group-stage games. A United States player was sent off, and FIFA later suspended the ban that had been expected. UEFA and other football bodies criticised that decision.

questions.q: In which city was the Argentina–Algeria match played, the game in which Lionel Messi made World Cup history?
questions.explanation: That match was played in Kansas City, Missouri.

questions.q: Who scored the winning goal when Spain won its first World Cup, in the 2010 final?
questions.explanation: Andrés Iniesta scored the winning goal in Spain's 1-0 extra-time win over the Netherlands.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Spain was the first team to win the World Cup while conceding only one goal in the tournament.
Reason (R): Spain was the first nation to be reigning champion of both the men's and women's World Cups.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the second does not explain the first.

questions.explanation: Messi played at six World Cups, Ronaldo scored in six consecutive editions, Ochoa made a sixth straight squad, and Italy failed to qualify.

II. Lionel Messi is the only player to have won the Golden Ball twice.

questions.explanation: Spain's first title came in 2010, not 1998.

questions.q:

II. Spain's first World Cup title came in 1934.
III. Cristiano Ronaldo was the first player to score in five consecutive World Cups.

questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct; Spain's first title came in 2010 and Ronaldo's run covered six consecutive editions.

questions.q: In which year did India have its only World Cup qualification?
questions.explanation: India's only qualification came in 1950, but the team withdrew before the tournament in Brazil.
